data.title: Braemar Hotels & Resorts Appoints Seven New Directors
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Braemar Hotels & Resorts appointed seven new directors following the resignation of its board.

The real estate investment trust said the directors and Chief Executive Richard Stockton will stand for election at the annual meeting on Dec. 21. At the new board's first meeting, it is expected to appoint Stephen Haggerty as its independent chair.

The seven directors resigned from the board following the company's transition into a self-managed real estate investment trust.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com

data.title: Twenty One Capital Purchases an Additional $10 Million Worth of Bitcoin, Increasing Holdings to Approximately 43,841 BTC
data.description:
Twenty One Capital, Inc. ("Twenty One" or "XXI") () today announced the purchase of 172.25 bitcoin for $10 million, at an average purchase price of approximately $58,054 per bitcoin. The purchase was funded with cash, and brings the Company’s total holdings to approximately 43,841 bitcoin as of November 20, 2026.

“We purchased another $10 million of Bitcoin today, bringing our purchases this week to $20 million,” said Rapha Zagury, Chief Executive Officer of Twenty One. “Market downturns are part of Bitcoin’s history, and they create opportunities for investors with a long-term perspective. We have been deliberate about when to buy and the recent market decline gave us an attractive opportunity to put some cash to work. We’ll continue to build Twenty One with discipline and conviction.”

This purchase follows the company’s November 16 announcement of 154.32 bitcoin, bringing total purchases across both announcements to 326.57 bitcoin. Twenty One plans to make additional Bitcoin purchases, which is core to the company’s strategy, with the amount and timing determined by market conditions, available liquidity, and competing investment opportunities.

About Twenty One

Twenty One is a Bitcoin-focused operating company. Designed to pair one of the largest Bitcoin treasuries in the public markets with operating businesses, Twenty One aims to provide shareholders with direct, capital-efficient exposure to Bitcoin through a growing Bitcoin-native platform. For more information, visit https://twentyonecapital.com/investors.

These forward-looking statements are based on management's current expectations. These statements are neither promises nor guarantees, but involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other important factors that may cause actual future events, results, or achievements to be materially different from the Company's expectations and projections expressed or implied by the forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements speak only as of the date of this press release, and Twenty One assumes no obligation to update such forward-looking statements, except as required by law.

Such disclosures will be included on Twenty One's website. data.title: NI Holdings Approves $5M Buyback
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

NI Holdings approved an authorization to buy back $5 million shares.

The new program supports the insurance company's approach to capital deployment to create value for shareholders, NI said.

The previous buyback program, which was approved in August 2025, has been fully utilized.

NI Holdings had more than 20.3 million shares as of Oct. 31.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Anthropic Barely Dodges Broken IPO Status — Market Talk
data.description: A day after snagging the "biggest ever" initial public offering crown from SpaceX, Anthropic very nearly picks up the more dubious distinction of biggest ever broken IPO. An IPO is considered broken if a stock trades below its offering price shortly after the offering. Anthropic shares end the day down 8.5% at $88.91 after falling to as low as $83.05, nearly breaking its $83 IPO price. SpaceX shares, priced at $135 in June, reached a high of $225.64 shortly after the IPO before falling below $135 the following month and closing Friday at $127.79. The 10 biggest U.S. IPOs this year prior to Anthropic's were trading on average more than 20% below their offer prices, the Financial Times reported earlier this week. (colin.kellaher@wsj.com)

data.title: Maverick Gold and Silver Announces Closing of Final Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Maverick Gold and Silver Corp., (FSE: VR61) (OTC Pink: VRCFF) ("Maverick" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has closed the final tranche (the "Final Tranche") of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 8, 2026 and October 16, 2026 (the "Offering"). Under the Final Tranche, the Company issued 2,000,000 units (each, a "Unit") at a price of C$0.05 per Unit for gross proceeds of C$100,000.

Together with the first tranche, the Company has issued a total of 13,080,000 Units under the Offering for aggregate gross proceeds of C$654,000.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. The Units were offered to purchasers in reliance on available prospectus exemptions under applicable Canadian securities laws.

Offering Terms

Each Unit consists of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one additional Common Share at a price of C$0.10 for 24 months from the date of issuance. If, at any time prior to the expiry of the Warrants, the closing price of the Common Shares on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") equals or exceeds C$0.15 per Common Share for a period of 10 consecutive trading days, the Company may, at its option, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving written notice to the holders thereof, and in such case, the Warrants will expire on the 30th day after the date on which such notice is given by the Company.

In connection with the financing, the Company paid finders' fees totaling C$22,000 in cash and issued an aggregate of 440,000 non-transferable warrants (the "Finder Warrants") to certain eligible finders. Each Finder Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one Common Share at a price of C$0.10 for 24 months from the date of issuance.

All securities issued in connection with the Final Tranche are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, expiring March 21, 2027, in accordance with applicable securities legislation.

The securities issued pursuant to the Offering have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any applicable state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor will there be any sale of the securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Zooz Strategy said its board extended its share-repurchase program for an additional 12 months.
